Vitalik Buterin Unveils Privacy-Focused AI Agent Setup Combining zkAPI, Tor, and Local LLMs Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin showcased his personal privacy-focused AI agent setup, integrating zkAPI, Tor, random cover traffic, and local LLM prompt rewriting into the pi agent harness. The system assigns each conversation a separate Tor circuit, uses zkAPI to protect payment privacy, and rewrites prompts locally with a Qwen model. Vitalik said the setup is becoming usable but still suffers from significant latency, especially when starting new conversations, while Tor remains vulnerable to timing-correlation attacks involving colluding providers and entry nodes. He suggested that a specialized mixnet may offer stronger protection and added that lower gas costs for zkAPI deposits and withdrawals on Ethereum mainnet are coming soon. — link

Circle Reports $1.4 Billion in H1 2026 Revenue, With 59% Going to USDC Partners and Transaction Costs Circle disclosed that it generated approximately $1.4 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026, of which $819 million (59%) went to USDC distribution partners and transaction costs. Another $473 million (34%) was spent on licensing, banking relationships, settlement liquidity, compliance, and product development, leaving approximately 7% as net profit. Circle also stated that customers using the Circle Payments Network (CPN) and eligible Circle Platform customers can now access free, near-real-time USDC redemptions around the clock. USDC recorded more than $36 trillion in on-chain transaction volume in H1 2026, accounting for approximately 77% of global stablecoin transaction volume in June, according to Circle. — link

Cobo Wallet, One of the Early Crypto Wallet Apps Launched by F2Pool Co-Founder, to Shut Down Digital asset custody provider Cobo announced that its Cobo Wallet App will shut down on December 1 as part of a strategic business adjustment. Users must withdraw all assets by November 30 at 11:59 PM (UTC+8). Any remaining assets will incur a monthly management fee of 2%, with a minimum charge of $100. Accounts holding less than $100 will have their entire remaining balance deducted. The first fee will be charged on January 1, 2027, and fees will continue until all assets are withdrawn or depleted. Cobo emphasized that its other businesses will remain unaffected and continue operating normally. — link
